nodes.label: terrain
nodes.comment: One elevation field drives everything downstream: the land layer, the river courses, and where towns can appear all read this same node, so they always agree.

nodes.label: sea & land
nodes.comment: Base layer painting every cell: ocean below 0.45, grass above. The rivers node uses the same 0.45 as its sea level so river mouths land exactly on this coastline.

nodes.label: rivers
nodes.comment: Springs on ground above 0.62 flow down the steepest path with a little meander until they hit sea level. Painted with the water tile so rivers and ocean read as one body of water.

nodes.label: towns
nodes.comment: Reads the rivers and the same terrain: a town candidate is any river cell touching the sea (a mouth) or with three river neighbors (a junction), thinned to one town per 14 tiles.
